mechanism: Ketorolac may increase anticholinergic effects of meclizine and both drugs can cause CNS depression; ketorolac also increases GI bleeding risk which meclizine's anticholinergic properties may mask.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation) and CNS depression; use lowest effective doses and consider alternative antiemetics; assess GI bleeding risk given ketorolac's ulcerogenic potential.
